0.text:
Async Swap is an on-chain order book and matching engine built as a Uniswap v4 hook. Traders set a
limit price for assets paired with USDC. Orders match with other traders or with the pool's active
liquidity, and anyone can permissionlessly fill a resting order. Price, then bid, then time. Book matching ranks orders by price. Among orders at the same
price, a higher escrowed USDC priority bid goes first, and earlier orders break equal bids.Orders rest until they execute. Unfilled amounts stay open for later matching, a pool fill,
a filler, repricing or cancellation.No swap touches the curve directly. Every swap becomes an order. The only AMM swaps are the
ones the hook makes to fill a resting order from pool liquidity, and those pay active LPs
0.02% and the protocol 0.01%. Book matches and filler fills take 0.02% of what each side receives.Proceeds you can always claim. A book match credits both sides as PoolManager claims, which
you redeem to any address through TokenClaims (ERC-20) or NativeClaims (ETH). A recipient a
token refuses cannot block matching.

177.text:
Maker submits a new async order. userData must encode AsyncSwap.UserParams
with executor == address(this) so the router is authorized to fill later.
userData.amountOutMin MUST equal order.amountOutMin — the router enforces
this so the limit price the maker signs in order is exactly what beforeSwap
stores via hookData. The hook auto-assigns a salt on create and emits it in AsyncOrderCreated.
Submitters can pass order.salt = bytes32(0) on initial submission; the
field is only read on cancel / updatePrice / fill paths (where the maker
supplies the salt fetched from the indexer or event log). Native input (currency0 = address(0) and zeroForOne = true, OR currency1 =
address(0) and zeroForOne = false) requires msg.value == order.amountIn —
the router holds the ETH and settles it to PM during unlock. For ERC20 input
the maker must approve the router for amountIn of the input token. function swap(AsyncOrder calldata order, bytes memory userData) external payable; Parameters NameTypeDescriptionorderAsyncOrderuserDatabytes

178.text:
Filler completes an open order, paying exactly the maker's live minimum. The maker
receives it less the 0.02% trade fee, and the filler the input less 0.02%.
For ERC20 output, approve the router for that amount. For native output,
msg.value must equal the live minimum;
a stale or excessive deposit reverts rather than stranding the difference.
Native output is currency1 for zeroForOne, otherwise currency0. maxPrice caps the output the filler pays —
it protects fillers from a maker who front-runs them with updatePrice to
bump the order's stored price. Pass type(uint256).max to disable the check.
order.amountIn is the least input the filler accepts: the fill reverts if the
order's live input has dropped below it (e.g. after a partial match). function fillOrder(AsyncOrder calldata order, uint256 maxPrice, bytes calldata) external payable; Parameters NameTypeDescriptionorderAsyncOrdermaxPriceuint256_bytes

386.text:
A large order that fills against pool liquidity moves the pool price. Whoever trades the price back
earns the difference: a backrun. With only a static fee, that profit goes entirely to the
backrunner, and the LPs whose liquidity absorbed both trades lose it. Since v1.1.0, dynamic fee
ordering charges a pool fill that moves the price back a dynamic fee sized to the gap it closes,
and splits it between the LPs and the protocol. The dynamic fee applies only to pool fills (fillFromPoolLiquidity, including the pool attempt when a
new order arrives). Book matches and filler fills settle at the orders' signed limits, move no pool
price and don't pay it.
386.title: Dynamic fee ordering

387.text:
The logic is in DynamicFeeOrdering.sol, a linked library
that AsyncMatching calls after every pool fill. Reference. Each pool stores a reference tick and the block it was set in
(AsyncFiller.State.refTick, refBlock). The first pool fill after the window has expired records
the pool's tick from before that fill as the new reference, and pays no dynamic fee.Window. The reference holds for ORDERING_WINDOW = 2 blocks after the block that set it. A
pool fill after that starts a new window.Dynamic fee. A pool fill inside the window that ends closer to the reference than it started
paysfee = min(amountOut × (gapBefore + gapAfter) / 40_000, amountOut / 2)where gapBefore and gapAfter are the distances, in ticks, from the reference to the pool's tick
before and after the fill. If the fill crosses the reference, gapAfter is 0: the part past the
reference closes no gap. One tick is about 0.01%, so (gapBefore + gapAfter) / 2 is the average
price gap over the fill in basis points, and the fee is half the price gap the fill closes.No dynamic fee for a fill that moves the price further from the reference, or doesn't move it.Split. Half the dynamic fee is donated to in-range LPs (PoolManager.donate). The other half,
plus any rounding, is credited to the FeeVault as ERC-6909 claims. If no liquidity is in range
after the fill, all of it goes to the FeeVault.Maker protection. The dynamic fee is taken from the fill's output before the maker is paid, and
the output that remains must still meet the order's minimum. Otherwise the pool fill reverts, and
the order goes to the book or rests, exactly as when a pool fill misses its limit for any other
reason. The 0.01% protocol fee on the input and the 0.02% LP fee still apply to every pool fill; the dynamic
fee is on top of them. Each charge emits DynamicFeeCharged(poolId, orderId, currency, toLps, toFeeVault, refTick) from the
hook: the fill's output currency, the LPs' and the FeeVault's shares, and the reference tick it was
measured against. The fill's AsyncOrderLiquidityFilled reports the maker's output after the fee.

389.text:
A fee charged per swap invites splitting: several small backruns each pay a lower rate. Here the
dynamic fee depends on the gap at each fill's start and end, not on how many fills there are.

difference comes from averaging the gap linearly in ticks while the pool's price curve is not linear.

The dynamic fee is taken in the fill's output currency; the maker's minimum must still be met after it. Fills that move the price further from the reference, and fills after the window, pay none. Every fee the hook moves is logged by the hook, with its pool, so indexers never have to recompute fees from gross amounts: FeeEventLogged against0.02% trade fee, book matchOrderFeeAccrued(poolId, orderId, currency, amount), one per sidethe buy order (asset fee) and the sell order (quote fee)0.02% trade fee, filler fillOrderFeeAccrued, one per sidethe filled order: the maker's fee in the output, the filler's in the input0.01% protocol fee, pool fillOrderFeeAccruedthe filled order, in the inputDynamic fee, pool fillDynamicFeeCharged(poolId, orderId, currency, toLps, toFeeVault, refTick)the filled order, in the output0.02% LP fee, pool fillPoolManager's Swap event (fee)the pool AsyncOrdersMatched and AsyncOrderFilled carry gross amounts; AsyncOrderLiquidityFilled carries the maker's output after the dynamic fee. Priority bids are escrowed as hook claims by addOrder and settle to the FeeVault: the filled share as input fills, the rest when the order closes. They never go to LPs, so liquidity added just before a settlement earns none of them. An order-to-order match pays both sides, and returns any remainder left below the pool minimum, as PoolManager claims rather than token transfers, so a recipient a token refuses cannot block matching. Holders redeem ERC-20 claims through TokenClaims and native claims through NativeClaims, to any recipient, after approving the redeemer for that claim id. Filler fills and LP fills pay the maker's ERC-20 output directly. Minting bid claims creates hook debt immediately; the PoolManager unlock must settle that debt, including for custom executors. The Router pays it with settleFor(hook). All pools rank equal prices by remaining bid, then sequence. There is no FIFO mode or mode switch. The accounting invariant is fuzzed by the matching invariant suites: the hook's claim balance for each currency equals the sum of remaining inputs of open orders plus escrowed bids, and nothing is created or destroyed by a match. The hook's own token balance is zero between transactions, so sweep can only move stranded ETH or tokens sent to the hook by mistake, never escrow.

402.text:
Every resting order is indexed on its pool's book by a uint128 price key computed in
AsyncFiller._priceKey (TickPrice.key): the Uniswap v4 tick of the order's exact limit. Take the order's currency1/currency0 ratio: amountOutMin / amountIn when it sells currency0,
amountIn / amountOutMin when it sells currency1.Take its floor tick: the largest tick t (spacing 1, price 1.0001^t) priced at or below the
ratio (TickPrice.floorTick, via TickMath.getTickAtSqrtPrice).Order ticks by numeraire per asset: t - MIN_TICK + 1 when the numeraire is currency1,
MAX_TICK - t + 1 when it is currency0. Keys run from 1 to 2 * MAX_TICK + 1. Ratios outside the v4 price range (about 2^-128 to
2^128) share the end keys. Each level is 0.01% wide at any price and for any token decimals,
so two orders sharing a nonclamped key are within approximately 0.01% of each other.
The end levels do not have this spread bound. The exact limit stays on the order:
keys order the radix tree; they do not by themselves decide whether two orders trade.

403.title: Price keys

404.text:
AsyncMatching._crosses(buyKey, sellKey, buy, sell) decides whether a buy and a sell can trade: buyKey > sellKey is a cross and buyKey < sellKey is not. The key is monotone in the exact
price, so a strict ordering of keys always reflects a strict ordering of exact prices.Equal keys are decided at full precision: cross  <=>  buyIn / buyOut >= sellOut / sellIn
       <=>  buyIn * sellIn >= sellOut * buyOut
       <=>  floor(buyIn * sellIn / sellOut) >= buyOut      (sellOut and buyOut are nonzero) implemented as Math.mulDiv(buy.amountIn, sell.amountIn, sell.amountOutMin) >= buy.amountOutMin.
Orders cannot be created or updated with a zero minimum, so the divisor is never zero. Both escrowed inputs are bounded by signed 128-bit settlement amounts, so their product and
its quotient by a positive minimum fit in 256 bits, including at clamped end levels. An exact tie (buyIn * sellIn == sellOut * buyOut) counts as a cross and executes.
404.title: Crossing rule

405.text:
Equal-key noncrossing heads no longer terminate selection when another pair is eligible.
Each priority subtree stores its minimum exact ask or maximum exact bid. The search chooses
the higher-priority child if its summary admits a crossing order, otherwise the other child.
Each lookup traverses at most 128 branches without scanning or persistent cursors.Automatic arrivals and resting-book matching use the same selection rule: the exact highest
bid and exact lowest ask in their best levels. The subtree extremum is the eligibility threshold,
so only orders at that exact extremum qualify; remaining fee and sequence break exact-price ties.
If these extrema do not cross, no pair at the boundary crosses. Prices grouped in the same level
never let a worse exact price jump ahead by paying more.Every genuine cross, including the tie, produces a non-zero match in _matchAmounts that pays
each maker at least their signed minimum for the input consumed. This was checked exhaustively
for small amounts and on randomized large near-tie pairs.Matching compares the signed minimums, not the post-fee proceeds, so the 0.02% trade fee (taken
from each side's proceeds afterwards, rounded up) never changes which orders cross. Example of equal keys without a cross: a sell asking 1000.05 and a buy offering 1000.02
USDC per asset sit on the same tick, but the buy is below the ask, so the pair rests.
405.title: Consequences

407.text:
Within one tick, priority is bid then sequence, not exact price, so a higher-bid order can trade
ahead of one priced up to 0.01% better. Across ticks, price always comes first. Under the earlier
WAD-ratio key a level was 10^(assetDecimals - usdcDecimals - 18) USDC/asset wide, which is
about 10% of the price for an 18-decimal asset at $0.00001, and the clamped keys 1 and
type(uint128).max merged arbitrarily distant prices (audit 2026-10-23, finding 1). Ticks remove
both: the width is relative and fixed, and only prices outside the v4 range share the end keys.
407.title: Level width and the price-priority bound

408.text:
test/security/CoarsePriceBlocking.t.sol creates a pool with an 18-decimal asset and 6-decimal
USDC fixture at 1,000 USDC/asset, minimum order 1 USDC, and no active LP liquidity. A sell
offering 2e15 - 1 asset base units for 2_000_000 USDC base units has the same key as a
1,000 USDC/asset order, but a slightly higher exact ask. Its 100_001-unit bid outranks the
100_000-unit bids of 20 honest sells. Under the previous head-only policy, twenty matching buys stopped at that blocker, and 100
retries made no progress. The Python legacy_matching=True mode preserves that baseline. With exact eligibility, the same twenty buys execute against the honest sells without cancelling
or outbidding the blocker. The blocker remains open, preserving its escrow and bid. The updated
CoarsePriceBlockingTest asserts that outcome through the real Router/hook/PoolManager, and tests
the mirrored incoming-sell case. Generated EligiblePythonVectors.t.sol exercises normal prices,
both clamps, blockers on both sides, mutations, partial fills, balances and fee claims. With tick keys the blocker above is one level worse than the honest asks, so it cannot outrank
them at all. A level is 0.01% of the price wide. That bounds price separation, not delay or backlog.
The repaired selector guarantees finding a crossing pair in a valid book when one exists;
successful settlement and transaction submission remain required. It does not guarantee that
every low-priority order eventually fills under continuing higher-priority arrivals. The companion model is in the local uv4 checkout under src/uv4/priority_protocol/, with results
and explicit modeling boundaries in docs/priority_protocol/. PriorityPythonVectors.t.sol checks
100 independently generated Python matching cases against the real matcher;
PriorityPythonHashes.t.sol checks order identities and signature struct hashes.
408.title: Historical counterexample and repaired regression

409.text:
EligiblePrice.sol compares full 512-bit cross products and stores two-word exact bounds at
priority-tree nodes. Append/remove repair the affected ancestor path. Every partial fill refreshes
the bound even if neither the tick key nor the remaining fee changes. New storage is appended
to each price level; existing live trees would need their summaries initialized before using this
code. These local changes have not been deployed. The protocol-controlled index work is O(128 M) for M matches. Eight is the existing per-call cap,
not a per-transaction cap. Token code and external settlement costs are outside this structural
bound. EligibleGas.t.sol measures composed batches through a real unlock; no numerical
worst-case gas certificate or universally optimal batch size is claimed. The updated whitepaper is in the local asyncswap/whitepaper checkout. Its new section contains
integer safety and search arguments, gas curves, and the constrained parameter objective.

412.text:
An ERC-20 payout runs the token's code while the PoolManager is still unlocked, and the hook's own
entry points (cancelOrder by the owner, matchBook, updatePrice, executeOrder by an executor)
are callable from there. The order must already be closed or reduced when that code runs. AsyncFiller.fill: the order is removed, deleted and its paid bid settled (_closeOrder) before
the maker's output, the fee and the filler's input are paid.AsyncMatching.fillFromPoolLiquidity: the order is removed and deleted before the pool swap and the
maker's payout.AsyncMatching._matchPair: recipients are read first (_payouts), both orders are reduced, then
the two escrow legs pay out (_settleTransfers). Since the fix for 9, those legs credit PoolManager
claims and run no token code at all. Tests: test/nethermind_auditagent/NethermindAuditAgent.t.sol

(a token notifies the paid maker, which only reads the order's record) and

412.title: 1, 2: order state is final before any payout

413.text:
EligiblePrice augments each priority radix tree with exact subtree price extrema. A lookup
returns the highest-fee, earliest-sequence order that crosses the counterparty in at most 128
branches. Noncrossing heads remain open and no longer hide eligible lower-priority orders.
For a resting equal-key book, selection maximizes buy priority first, then eligible sell priority.
Append/remove and every live partial fill maintain the extrema, including unchanged-key/fee fills. The original approximately 2-USDC blocker no longer stalls 20,000 USDC of executable orders.
CoarsePriceBlockingTest covers both incoming directions. EligiblePythonVectors.t.sol compares
514 operations and 132 matches against an independent rational-price Python oracle, including
both clamps, two-sided blockers, mutations, selected IDs, remainders, fees, and maker balances.
EligiblePriceTest checks subtree invariants, randomized mutations, full depth, and node reuse. The index bound is independent of blocker count. Matching runs no token code (finding 9), so a
blocker cannot make it revert or burn gas through a payout. See docs/price-key-crossing.md and the
revised whitepaper for the argument.
413.title: 3: exact eligibility inside coarse price buckets

414.text:
AsyncFiller.settlePriorityFee no longer checks in-range liquidity: every settled bid (the filled
share on a match, the rest on close, cancel, fill or pool fill) is burned from the hook's claims and
minted to the FeeVault. Liquidity added for the moment of settlement receives none of it. (Active
LPs still earn the 30 bps fill fee on a pool fill, as on any Uniswap swap; that fee is not a bid.) Tests: test_M4_liquidityAddedBeforeFillGetsNoBid (on the audited code the bid shows up as LP fee

AsyncMatching.matchIncoming now runs matchBook on the whole book, within the same 8-match budget,

AsyncMatching._transferEscrow credits ERC-6909 claims in every currency, for both escrow legs and
for a remainder returned below the pool minimum. Holders redeem with the new TokenClaims
(redeem(currency, recipient, amount), after approving it on the PoolManager), to any recipient the
token accepts. A recipient the token refuses therefore cannot revert a match. Fills by a filler and pool-liquidity fills still pay the maker in ERC-20. A refused maker can only
fail its own order there: the pool fill runs behind a caught self-call and leaves the order resting,
and a filler fill reverts for that one order. Tests: test_M9_blockedRecipientDoesNotBlockMatch (on the audited code the refused transfer reverts

Found while fixing 1 and 2. _beforeSwap puts the order on the book before the Router pulls the

423.text:
Async Swap targets institutional-size orders; small trades are better served by the AMM. Measured in
numeraire (USDC) base units: Minimum order. Each pool has a minimum (setMinOrder(key, amount), owner only); pools start with
the hook's defaultMinOrder (setDefaultMinOrder). script/01_DeployHook.s.sol sets it to $10
(DEPLOY_MIN_ORDER_USD, scaled by the numeraire's decimals()). A buy's input must be at least the
minimum; a sell's minimum output must be, and so must its input valued at the pool's current price,
which keeps out sells that ask for the minimum but offer almost nothing. updatePrice re-checks it.
The pool price is an estimate: an empty pool still shows its creation price, so this is an admission
gate, not an oracle.Remainders. A partial match that leaves an order worth less than the minimum, by its own terms
(no pool price), closes it and returns the remaining input as claims after both orders are reduced.Tiered bid. The least bid is min($0.10, 0.1% of the order): $0.10 from $100 up, down to $0.01
at the $10 minimum. Tests: test/security/MinimumOrder.t.sol, including a sell and a buy remainder refunded below the
minimum, and the value check on a pool whose numeraire is currency0. Formal tests updated: the addOrder and CreateOrderSpec
fee guards, and beforeInitialize's write set (now also priceBooks[id].minOrder). Hook size: updatePriceWithSig called the internal AsyncFiller.updatePrice, inlining it into the
hook; it now goes through the linked AsyncMatching.updatePrice like updatePrice. AsyncSwap went
from 24,311 to about 20,200 bytes (EIP-170 limit 24,576).
423.title: Minimum order and tiered bid

424.text:
Findings 7 and 12 are fixed in the working tree. Every pool queues equal-price orders by
escrowed bid, then sequence. FIFO mode, its links, setOrderingMode, orderingMode, and the separate
recordPriorityFee call are removed. orderBookOrder now returns sequence and priorityFee in
its final two fields instead of FIFO neighbors; clients must update their ABI. addOrder mints the bid's numeraire claims to the hook immediately. This creates a matching hook
debt in PoolManager; the unlock cannot finish until it is settled. The Router pays it with
settleFor(hook). A custom executor cannot leave an order resting with an unpaid declared bid.
The tiered minimum still rounds down in base units, so a tiny order can have a zero minimum when
the pool minimum permits it. This change does not impose a universal $10 minimum. Tests: test/security/PriorityFeeOnly.t.sol checks minimum bids on unconfigured pools, bid ordering,
rejection of an executor that skips payment, successful paid custom execution, equal-bid time ordering,
and removal of the mode setter. Existing placement,
settlement, cancellation and invariant fixtures now account for escrowed bids. This changes storage layout and public ABI; deploy fresh contracts and update consumers. It is not
a migration of existing orders or deployed contracts.
